norms.what: A stage skill is model-invocable so the orchestrator can start it, which also lets Claude invoke it on an unrelated task; the run-file guard makes that cost one skill load. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39). In 0.6.0 the run's files moved from `.claude/audits/` to their own folder under `.model-audits/`: Claude Code protects all of `.claude/` from writes in every permission mode but bypass, and allow rules do not pre-approve them, so a headless smoke run in `acceptEdits` stopped before the plan and every user outside auto mode got a prompt per write (#57).
After compaction the orchestrator, the oldest skill of the run, is the first to be dropped; re-invoking it restores the run's standing rules. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Discovery rests on today's docs, not a table written months ago. WebFetch runs the page through a small model and returns its answer, which cannot support a verbatim passage; the docs serve raw Markdown at `<page>.md`, which `curl` reads. Offline, the recorded passages are the only docs left, and every finding says they were not re-verified. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39). In 0.6.0 the run's files moved from `.claude/audits/` to their own folder under `.model-audits/`: Claude Code protects all of `.claude/` from writes in every permission mode but bypass, and allow rules do not pre-approve them, so a headless smoke run in `acceptEdits` stopped before the plan and every user outside auto mode got a prompt per write (#57). After grading a full-scope run of `main` (a289710) on a seeded project against its sealed answer key — recall 96.6% primary, 89.8% strict, precision 100% — the run left a doc page and its normalised copy at the audited project's root, written by commands with paths relative to the working directory, while the report called the tree clean; every path is now absolute under the run's folder (#61). Discovery used to fetch each page with `curl`, with WebFetch as a fallback, and write its own digest (the retired `N04` and `N05`). It now reads the change digest that ships with the transition, written once by the maintainers with a passage per change (#106) and compared with the pages weekly in CI (#107). Since #105 the audit reaches no network: the directory's validation flagged the run-time fetch, and what a published plugin reads has to be in the reviewed commit.

One brief shared by every agent keeps them classifying alike; agents never see the session, and those that set `omitClaudeMd` do not load the project memory, so the facts they need arrive as quoted `file:line` text, never as a paraphrase that could be wrong. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N40` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N40` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39). In 0.6.0 the run's files moved from `.claude/audits/` to their own folder under `.model-audits/`: Claude Code protects all of `.claude/` from writes in every permission mode but bypass, and allow rules do not pre-approve them, so a headless smoke run in `acceptEdits` stopped before the plan and every user outside auto mode got a prompt per write (#57). In 0.6.2 the brief carries the lines of `unquoted.md` as `file:line | id | label`, never their text, so every agent knows which lines not to read (#87). The brief names the shipped change digest's path and no doc cache, which no run has (#108).

Writing each batch's lines before reading the next keeps no finding dependent on context that compaction could drop, and lets a resume tell which batches are done. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N08` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N08` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39). In 0.6.2 the order became strict: a batch's lines are written before anything else is opened, a skill read as context or a lead included. In the live run of #87 the agents batch's lines were still unwritten when [N21] opened the skills it preloads, and one refusal lost two batches.

Parallel auditors finish a large inventory sooner; they pin their own model and effort, and Claude Code refuses spawns above its concurrent limit, so they go in waves. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N40` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N40` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

The per-transition audits checked files against a closed pattern table, which acted as the boundary of the search: a capability evaluation measured 58% recall for the skill against 79% for a session given the doc links (#34). Judging against the docs finds what no table names, and requiring the passage behind each finding keeps the precision the table gave. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39). A finding now rests on a passage of the shipped digest, the only account of the docs a run reads, where it could rest on any passage of a fetched page; what the digest does not state, discovery cannot find, which is why the digest keeps a passage for every change it lists (#106, #108).

The items a closed inventory missed in that evaluation — a price table, a guide index, a version floor — each carry a token the docs name; searching the whole root for those tokens reaches them without listing them in advance. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Model-dependent behaviour can sit in a file the map does not name but a listed file points to; following leads within an approved budget keeps discovery open and its cost bounded. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

A file pinned to a third model is outside the transition; judging it against the target's docs would produce findings about the wrong model. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N10` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N10` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Signal words also appear in prose about other things, which produced false findings in early runs. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N41` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N41` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

An instruction outdated before the source model is outside this transition's evidence; reporting it as residue, with no change, keeps the audit within what its sources support. The examples differ per transition, so they come from the knowledge file. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N11` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N11` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39). In 0.6.1 a residue line needs a passage showing the instruction was written for a model older than the source: the 2026-09-29 capability evaluation of the Opus 5 → 5.5 transition graded a residue line with no passage as a false positive, and residue lines whose passage the project had already weighed in a decision record as unsupported, so the second kind is now `already decided` (#77). The passage that shows an instruction is older residue used to come from the source model's guide, fetched at run time; it now comes from the digest's `<older_residue>` block (#106, #108).

An audit that proposes removing a safety rule or a measured-failure rule does harm, whatever the docs say about tone or wording. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N12` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N12` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Anthropic's `claude-api` skill migrates request code with the right syntax for each SDK and platform, so the audit hands API findings off rather than editing them. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N25` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N25` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

A frontmatter `description` routes the skill or agent; urgency there is legitimate and not an instruction to the model about how to work. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N26` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N26` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Confidence tells the user how much to trust each finding; a system card describes an evaluation, not a rule, so a finding resting on it alone is low and cited by page and section. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N27` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N27`; `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N62` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Stretching a passage to fill a report costs the user's trust and time. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N28` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N28` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

A project that already decided for the target should see that decision respected, with where it says so. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N31` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N31` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39). In 0.6.2 (#86), the one false positive of the 0.6.1 suite was a docs file proposing a change to a Sonnet 5 fallback variable that the same file explains at a nearby line; the docs bear that reason out, but the norm cleared only what the project states it evaluated for the target. A value kept on purpose for a reason the docs support is now `already decided` too. No findings file was kept, so which stage kept the change is inferred.

A skill listed under `skills:` is injected in full into the agent at startup, and a custom subagent loads the project memory unless `omitClaudeMd` is set, so an instruction stated there is not missing; a `disable-model-invocation` skill cannot be preloaded. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N58` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N58` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39). In 0.6.2 the preloaded skills are searched for the instruction with Grep, reading only the lines around a match, instead of being read in full inside the agents batch: the full read opened a second batch's worth of text before the first was written, and it held the lines that stopped the run on a refusal (#87).

Some techniques written for the source stay recommended for the target, and some settings serve the target's own fallback; flagging them would propose removing what the docs keep. The list is per transition, so it comes from the knowledge file. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N61` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39).

Open discovery must say what it did not read, or its silence reads as a clean result; the account also shows how the docs were read, so an offline run is never taken for a verified one. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #39). In 0.6.2 the coverage account names the lines skipped per [N25] and the files `not audited — refusal` per [transition-audit#N21] (#87). The coverage account used to say how the docs were read — raw, through WebFetch or from recorded passages; it now gives the date the digest was checked (#108).

Added in 0.6.1. In the 2026-09-29 capability evaluation of the Opus 5 → 5.5 transition one run dismissed a missing effort level because the auditor's own `~/.claude/settings.json` saved one for the target, and another kept a launch recipe with no effort flag as "inherited from what the user saved". The user settings file applies to that user on that machine; the other developers of the project, its CI and its headless runs never get it, so an audit that lets it settle a finding reports a configuration the project does not ship. The file stays context for explaining what the user sees today (#77).

In 0.6.2 (#87), a live session-mode run on the Sonnet fixture stopped mid-discovery with `stop_reason: "refusal"`, category `reasoning_extraction`, after reading the lines the reasoning-in-the-reply trap (Opus P04, Sonnet P09) exists to find; the guides say such requests can be declined, and Claude Code's automatic fallback covers other categories only, so the run simply stopped. Reading the file around the listed line keeps the rest of the file audited for every other trap, and the lines around it are enough to tell an instruction from prose ([N13]). A paraphrase the pattern misses is cited the same way once seen, so it is not quoted back; if reading it stops the run, [transition-audit#N21] recovers.
